# If a branch has been merged into its base,
# restack should detect this and skip it
# instead of attempting to rebase already-merged commits.
#
# Regression test for https://github.com/abhinav/git-spice/issues/314

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2024-03-30T14:59:32Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git commit --allow-empty -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init

# Set up a stack: main -> feat1 -> feat2
git add feat1.txt
gs bc feat1 -m 'Add feat1'

git add feat2.txt
gs bc feat2 -m 'Add feat2'

# Simulate a non-fast-forward merge of feat1 into main
# (like a GitHub "merge commit" merge).
# First make a change on main so it can't fast-forward.
gs bco main
cp $WORK/extra/main-change.txt .
git add main-change.txt
git commit -m 'Independent main commit'

# Now merge feat1 into main with a merge commit.
git merge feat1 --no-edit

# Go to feat2 and restack the stack.
git checkout feat2
gs stack restack
stderr 'feat1: branch appears to have been merged into main'
stderr 'repo sync'

-- repo/feat1.txt --
contents of feat1

-- repo/feat2.txt --
contents of feat2

-- extra/main-change.txt --
independent change on main
